stage_2_story.text_en:
Last summer, David and his family spent a wonderful day at a beautiful beach on the Mediterranean coast. The sun was shining and the sea was a deep shade of blue.

David's son, Noam, ran straight to the shore and began building an enormous sandcastle. He dug a moat around it and decorated it with shells — it was a masterpiece.

David put on his mask and snorkel and swam out to explore the coral reef nearby. He could not believe what he saw — dozens of colourful fish swimming between the coral. He stayed in the water for almost an hour.

His daughter, Maya, was less careful. She spent the whole morning lying in the sun reading a book and completely forgot to apply sunscreen. By lunchtime, her shoulders were bright red and very sore from the sunburn.

In the afternoon, the tide came in stronger than expected. The waves grew bigger and reached close to the shore. A lifeguard on duty noticed that Noam had wandered too deep and blew his whistle, waving him back to safety. David gave Noam a towel and a firm but kind talk about listening to the lifeguard.

Despite the sunburn and the exciting moment with the tide, the family agreed it had been a perfect beach day.
